laws.title: Speed Limit Enforcement
laws.content: Speed limits must be observed at all times. Exceeding posted limits may result in fines.

laws.title: Weapons Permit Required
laws.content: All firearms must be registered and carried with a valid permit.

laws.title: Business License Requirement
laws.content: All businesses must obtain and maintain a valid business license.

laws.title: Speed Limit Enforcement
laws.content: Speed limits must be observed at all times. Exceeding posted limits may result in fines.

laws.title: Weapons Permit Required
laws.content: All firearms must be registered and carried with a valid permit.

laws.title: Business License Requirement
laws.content: All businesses must obtain and maintain a valid business license.

laws.title: Active Shooter Response
laws.content:
Purpose: Provide immediate action steps to stop ongoing deadly threats.

Policy: Primary mission is to stop the threat; officers form contact teams and move to gunfire when safe to do so.

Procedure: 1) Arrive, assess, and move toward threat with minimum team.
2) Bypass wounded until threat stopped; relay locations.
3) Establish contact and rescue teams; coordinate with dispatch.
4) Transition to perimeter and handoff to investigative units.

Notes: Unified command with fire/EMS once scene stabilizes.

laws.title: Barricaded Suspects
laws.content:
Purpose: Outline containment and negotiation for barricades.

Policy: Priority is preservation of life; slow, controlled response with negotiators and specialty units as needed.

Procedure: 1) Establish perimeter and inner/outer containment.
2) Evacuate exposed civilians and isolate suspect.
3) Gather intel (weapons, mental health, layout).
4) Request negotiators/SWAT early when indicators present.
5) Document timeline and decisions for after-action.

Notes: Do not force entry unless exigency or authorized tactical plan.

laws.title: High-Risk Felony Stops
laws.content:
Purpose: Ensure controlled stops of high-risk vehicles.

Policy: Use multiple units, clear commands, and cover positions; occupants removed one at a time.

Procedure: 1) Coordinate location with cover units.
2) Position vehicles for cover and containment.
3) Issue PA commands; remove and secure occupants sequentially.
4) Clear vehicle before approach.
5) Document and tow per policy when needed.

Notes: Consider K-9 or air support when available.

laws.title: Officer Down Response
laws.content:
Purpose: Guide coordinated response to injured officers.

Policy: Closest units respond code; command establishes rescue plan, perimeter, and medical access.

Procedure: 1) Broadcast location, suspect info, and needs.
2) Form rescue team; move with cover to recover officer.
3) Provide immediate medical care and evacuate to EMS.
4) Secure scene for investigation and peer support.

Notes: Notify command staff as soon as practicable.

laws.title: Priority Call Handling
laws.content:
Purpose: Standardize response to high-priority incidents.

Policy: Response level matches call priority; supervisors may downgrade or upgrade based on conditions.

Procedure: 1) Monitor dispatch details and location.
2) Acknowledge en route with unit status.
3) Use lights/siren per driving policy when responding code.
4) Stage when appropriate and wait for cover.
5) Update dispatch with arrival, actions, and clearance.

Notes: Self-dispatching to high-priority calls requires notification.

laws.title: Body Camera Usage
laws.content:
Purpose: Provide consistent use of body-worn cameras for accountability.

Policy: BWCs are activated during enforcement, detentions, transports, and citizen contacts unless prohibited by law.

Procedure: 1) Verify camera operational at start of shift.
2) Activate before arrival on calls or immediately upon contact.
3) Verbally note when privacy requires deactivation; reactivate ASAP.
4) Tag uploads with incident identifiers before end of shift.

Notes: Follow state law for restricted locations and protected communications.

laws.title: Chain of Command
laws.content:
Purpose: Clarify how direction flows and how officers raise issues or approvals.

Policy: Personnel follow the established chain for directives, approvals, and grievances unless urgency demands immediate action.

Procedure: 1) Take routine direction from immediate supervisor.
2) Elevate critical issues to next level if supervisor unavailable.
3) Document requests for approvals (leave, training, equipment).
4) Notify command when bypassing steps for emergency reasons.

Notes: Use clear timestamps when escalating beyond normal order.

laws.title: Ethics and Integrity
laws.content:
Purpose: Reinforce honesty, impartiality, and avoidance of corruption.

Policy: Officers do not solicit gifts, falsify statements, or conceal evidence. Transparency with supervisors is mandatory.

Procedure: 1) Disclose gifts, secondary jobs, or relationships that may affect duty.
2) Accurately record actions and evidence.
3) Refuse preferential treatment requests; report attempts.
4) Immediately report corruption or integrity concerns.

Notes: Misrepresentation in reports or testimony is grounds for discipline.

laws.title: Officer Conduct and Professionalism
laws.content:
Purpose: Set expectations for demeanor, language, and professionalism when representing the department.

Policy: Officers shall treat all persons with respect, avoid discriminatory language, and follow department appearance and communication standards.

Procedure: 1) Maintain clean uniform and gear before shift.
  2) Use calm, clear, and respectful speech on all contacts.
  3) De-escalate tense interactions through tone and space.
  4) Report observed misconduct through the chain of command.

Notes: Applies on and off duty while identifying as law enforcement.

laws.title: On-Duty and Off-Duty Conduct
laws.content:
Purpose: Outline expected conduct while working and when identifiable as an officer off duty.

Policy: Officers act with integrity, avoid conflicts of interest, and do not misuse authority while off duty.

Procedure: 1) Do not consume intoxicants on duty.
2) Avoid enforcement while off duty unless life-threatening.
3) Identify conflicts (business, family, financial) early.
4) Notify supervision after any notable off-duty police action.

Notes: Seek supervisor guidance before off-duty security details.

laws.title: Complaint Handling
laws.content:
Purpose: Ensure public and internal complaints are recorded and investigated.

Policy: All complaints are accepted without delay; retaliation is prohibited; documentation is mandatory.

Procedure: 1) Accept complaint in any form; provide reference number.
2) Notify supervisor and IA channel per policy.
3) Preserve any evidence (video, documents).
4) Provide status updates through established process.

Notes: Anonymous complaints are documented and assessed equally.

laws.title: Internal Investigations
laws.content:
Purpose: Ensure fair, thorough investigations of misconduct.

Policy: Investigations are objective, timely, and documented; subjects are notified consistent with policy.

Procedure: 1) Assign investigator and scope; secure evidence.
2) Interview complainant, witnesses, and subject officer.
3) Analyze policy compliance and document findings.
4) Present findings to command for disposition.

Notes: Maintain confidentiality and protect against retaliation.

laws.title: Officer Involved Incidents
laws.content:
Purpose: Outline response to shootings, serious collisions, or critical events involving officers.

Policy: Involved officers are separated, statements managed per legal and contractual requirements, and support services offered.

Procedure: 1) Secure scene and evidence; assign investigators.
2) Separate involved and witness officers; assign peers.
3) Provide medical and wellness resources.
4) Follow critical incident protocol for interviews and relief from duty.

Notes: Union/employee rights are honored per agreements and law.

laws.title: Use of Force Review
laws.content:
Purpose: Standardize administrative review of force incidents.

Policy: Every reportable force event is reviewed for policy compliance by supervision and, when required, IA.

Procedure: 1) Officer submits force report and uploads media before end of shift when feasible.
2) Supervisor conducts interview and scene review.
3) Forward package to IA/command for final determination.
4) Track corrective actions or training needs.

Notes: Serious force may trigger parallel criminal and admin reviews.

laws.title: Crime Scene Management
laws.content:
Purpose: Protect scenes to preserve evidence and safety.

Policy: Officers establish inner/outer perimeters, log entry, and prevent unnecessary contamination.

Procedure: 1) Render aid and neutralize threats first.
2) Establish tape and a single entry point.
3) Start scene log and note initial conditions.
4) Await investigators; do not move evidence unless necessary.
5) Brief investigators with observations and actions taken.

Notes: Weather or crowds may justify rapid evidence protection measures.

laws.title: Evidence Collection and Handling
laws.content:
Purpose: Ensure evidence is lawfully collected, packaged, and tracked.

Policy: Chain of custody must be maintained with accurate labeling and submission.

Procedure: 1) Photograph evidence in place when safe.
2) Use gloves and appropriate packaging for item type.
3) Label with case number, location, collector, date/time.
4) Complete evidence entry and submit to property promptly.

Notes: Biological and digital evidence require special handling protocols.

laws.title: Interview and Interrogation
laws.content:
Purpose: Provide lawful, ethical questioning standards.

Policy: Miranda advisement is given when required; coercion, promises, or threats are prohibited.

Procedure: 1) Determine custody status and need for Miranda.
2) Record interviews when policy allows.
3) Ask open-ended questions; avoid leading promises.
4) Document verbatim statements when significant.

Notes: Provide breaks and basic needs to maintain voluntariness.

laws.title: Search and Seizure
laws.content:
Purpose: Guide lawful searches respecting constitutional limits.

Policy: Searches require warrant, consent, exigency, or other lawful exception; scope limited to justification.

Procedure: 1) Determine legal basis and document it.
2) Obtain written or recorded consent when applicable.
3) Limit search to areas authorized; stop when scope met.
4) Inventory seized items and provide receipts when required.

Notes: Consult supervisor or legal advisor for complex searches.

laws.title: Warrants and Affidavits
laws.content:
Purpose: Standardize preparation and execution of warrants.

Policy: Affidavits must be truthful, complete, and reviewed; execution follows knock-notice rules unless lawful exception.

Procedure: 1) Draft affidavit with probable cause and nexus clearly stated.
2) Obtain supervisory and prosecutorial review when required.
3) Brief team on layout, risks, and roles.
4) Execute warrant safely; record times and inventory items seized.

Notes: Return warrant and inventory to issuing authority promptly.

laws.title: Arrest Procedures
laws.content:
Purpose: Ensure arrests are lawful, safe, and documented.

Policy: Probable cause is required; force and restraints follow policy; arrestees are advised of rights when interrogated.

Procedure: 1) Confirm probable cause and articulate elements.
2) Handcuff, search, and secure weapons/evidence.
3) Advise Miranda when questioning post-custody.
4) Transport safely; complete booking paperwork and reports.

Notes: Medical clearance required if injury or complaint of pain.

laws.title: Field Interviews
laws.content:
Purpose: Standardize collection of information during investigative contacts.

Policy: Interviews are voluntary unless detained; officers must note demeanor, statements, and conditions.

Procedure: 1) Confirm whether the contact is voluntary or detained.
2) Ask concise questions tied to the observed activity.
3) Record identifiers and statements accurately.
4) Enter FI data into approved system before end of shift.

Notes: Parents/guardians should be notified when interviewing juveniles when practical.

laws.title: Pedestrian Stops
laws.content:
Purpose: Guide contact with pedestrians while respecting constitutional rights.

Policy: Officers must have reasonable suspicion for detentions and articulate the reason and duration.

Procedure: 1) Observe and form reasonable suspicion before detaining.
2) Identify yourself and the reason for the stop.
3) Conduct frisk only when articulable safety concerns exist.
4) Release promptly when suspicion is dispelled; document the stop.

Notes: Voluntary contacts remain consensual and may be ended by the subject.

laws.title: Prisoner Transport
laws.content:
Purpose: Provide safe, humane transport of persons in custody.

Policy: Vehicles are searched before/after transport; prisoners seat-belted and monitored.

Procedure: 1) Search prisoner and vehicle prior to loading.
2) Seat-belt and position to reduce risk of assault or escape.
3) Monitor during transport; advise dispatch of start/end mileage when policy requires.
4) Transfer custody with documentation and property inventory.

Notes: Opposite-sex transports require radio log and notification when possible.

laws.title: Report Writing Standards
laws.content:
Purpose: Maintain clear, timely, and accurate reports.

Policy: Reports must be objective, completed before end of shift unless approved extension, and include evidence references.

Procedure: 1) Use clear chronology and separate observations from statements.
2) Include elements of offenses and probable cause.
3) Reference body cam identifiers and evidence numbers.
4) Submit for supervisory review when required.

Notes: Proofread for spelling, dates, and identifiers before submission.

laws.title: Traffic Stop Procedures
laws.content:
Purpose: Provide safe, consistent approach to vehicle stops.

Policy: Stops are conducted with clear identification, radio updates, and adherence to officer safety and constitutional limits.

Procedure: 1) Radio location, plate, occupants if known.
2) Position patrol car safely; activate lights and camera.
3) Approach cautiously, identify yourself, and state reason.
4) Check warrants and documents; take action within policy.
5) Conclude with clear instructions and documentation.

Notes: Use two-officer approach when available on high-risk indicators.

laws.title: K-9 Deployment
laws.content:
Purpose: Set safe, lawful use of police canines.

Policy: Handlers control deployment; bites require medical care and reporting; announcements made when required.

Procedure: 1) Assess necessity (flight, hiding suspects, evidence search).
2) Give loud announcement before apprehension deployments when practical.
3) Maintain leash control unless directed otherwise.
4) Provide medical aid after contact and document deployment.

Notes: Avoid K-9 deployment on passive crowds or for mere non-compliance.

laws.title: Narcotics Operations
laws.content:
Purpose: Provide safeguards for undercover and narcotics enforcement.

Policy: Operations require supervisor approval, risk assessment, and adherence to informant handling rules.

Procedure: 1) Complete operational plan with objectives and contingencies.
2) Vet and document informant use.
3) Maintain surveillance teams and arrest contingencies.
4) Preserve evidence chain and submit for lab promptly.

Notes: Avoid buy/bust without cover and surveillance teams.

laws.title: SWAT Deployment
laws.content:
Purpose: Define when to request tactical team support.

Policy: SWAT is activated for high-risk operations exceeding patrol capabilities and requires command approval.

Procedure: 1) Identify high-risk factors (weapons, fortification, hostages).
2) Notify supervisor and command with facts.
3) Preserve perimeter and gather intel until team arrives.
4) Support unified command post once deployed.

Notes: Do not self-deploy into inner perimeter without assignment.

laws.title: Traffic Enforcement Operations
laws.content:
Purpose: Coordinate planned traffic safety details.

Policy: Operations focus on safety violations; citations and arrests follow standard procedures with data collection.

Procedure: 1) Brief team on location, goals, and legal considerations.
2) Use visible markings and cones when safe.
3) Track stops, warnings, and citations issued.
4) Debrief results and adjust tactics for future ops.

Notes: Coordinate with media or community outreach when appropriate.

laws.title: Field Training Program
laws.content:
Purpose: Define structure for training new officers.

Policy: FTOs follow approved curriculum, document daily performance, and provide timely feedback.

Procedure: 1) Orient trainee to equipment, policy, and expectations.
2) Use daily observation reports with specific examples.
3) Conduct mid-phase and end-phase evaluations.
4) Recommend advancement, extension, or remediation with justification.

Notes: FTO changes require supervisor approval.

laws.title: Firearms Qualification
laws.content:
Purpose: Ensure officers maintain firearms proficiency and safety.

Policy: All sworn personnel must qualify on issued weapons at required intervals; failure triggers remediation.

Procedure: 1) Attend scheduled qualification sessions.
2) Follow range safety rules and instructor commands.
3) Log scores and any malfunctions.
4) Complete remedial sessions until qualified or relieved of duty weapons.

Notes: Document alternative duty status if qualification is not met.

laws.title: Probationary Officer Standards
laws.content:
Purpose: Set expectations for probationary performance and milestones.

Policy: Probationers must meet training benchmarks, policy compliance, and attendance requirements.

Procedure: 1) Provide probation schedule and required competencies.
2) Meet regularly with supervisor and FTO for feedback.
3) Address deficiencies with written improvement plans.
4) Document completion or extension decisions in writing.

Notes: Failure to meet standards may result in separation.

laws.title: Remedial Training
laws.content:
Purpose: Offer structured remediation for identified performance gaps.

Policy: Supervisors may assign remedial training to address deficiencies before discipline when appropriate.

Procedure: 1) Identify specific deficiency and desired outcome.
2) Assign targeted training or mentoring with timeline.
3) Document completion and evaluate improvement.
4) Escalate if performance does not improve.

Notes: Serious misconduct may bypass remediation steps.

laws.title: Duty to Intervene
laws.content:
Purpose: Ensure officers act to stop unlawful or excessive force.

Policy: Officers must intervene and report when observing unreasonable force or misconduct regardless of rank.

Procedure: 1) Verbally direct the involved officer to stop.
2) Physically intervene if verbal direction fails and safe.
3) Render aid to affected persons.
4) Notify supervisor immediately and document incident.

Notes: Retaliation for intervention or reporting is prohibited.

laws.title: Firearm Discharge Policy
laws.content:
Purpose: Define when intentional firearm discharge is authorized.

Policy: Firearm use is restricted to defense of life or to stop serious bodily harm; warning shots are prohibited.

Procedure: 1) Point only when deadly force conditions may exist.
2) Consider backdrop and bystanders before firing.
3) Notify supervisor and secure scene after discharge.
4) Provide medical aid and preserve evidence.
5) Complete required reports and submit firearm for inspection.

Notes: Accidental discharges require immediate notification and review.

laws.title: Less-Lethal Weapons
laws.content:
Purpose: Set guidance for tasers, beanbag, OC, and similar tools.

Policy: Less-lethal options are used when reasonably necessary to gain compliance and when benefits outweigh risks.

Procedure: 1) Assess subject factors (age, health indicators, environment).
2) Provide warnings when practical.
3) Avoid sensitive areas (head, spine) unless deadly force would be justified.
4) After use, handcuff, monitor, and arrange medical evaluation.
5) Document cartridge numbers or munitions used.

Notes: Remove probes per medical protocol; photograph impacts.

laws.title: Use of Deadly Force
laws.content:
Purpose: Clarify deadly force threshold and responsibilities.

Policy: Deadly force is authorized only to protect life from imminent threat of death or serious injury and must cease once threat ends.

Procedure: 1) Confirm imminent threat; consider background and crossfire.
2) Issue commands when feasible.
3) Fire controlled rounds; reassess after each volley.
4) Provide medical aid and secure scene.
5) Notify command and cooperate with review.

Notes: Vehicle ramming is deadly force and follows same standard.

laws.title: Use of Force Continuum
laws.content:
Purpose: Explain proportional response options and expectations.

Policy: Force must be reasonable, necessary, and proportional to resistance, with de-escalation preferred when feasible.

Procedure: 1) Assess threat, severity, and subject behavior.
2) Attempt verbal de-escalation when safe.
3) Use lowest effective option; escalate only as needed.
4) Render aid after force and notify supervisor immediately.
5) Document and report per force reporting policy.

Notes: Early communication reduces need for higher force options.

laws.title: Air Support Coordination
laws.content:
Purpose: Leverage aviation assets to improve safety.

Policy: Air support is requested through dispatch or supervisor; ground units adjust tactics when air has visual.

Procedure: 1) Provide clear location, suspect description, and hazards.
2) Yield primary following role to air unit when overhead.
3) Use directed tactics (covert follow, perimeter guidance).
4) Maintain comms discipline on assigned channel.

Notes: Cancel ground pursuits when air can track safely when policy allows.

laws.title: Code 3 Driving
laws.content:
Purpose: Set rules for lights-and-siren responses.

Policy: Code 3 is authorized only for emergencies; due regard for safety is required at all times.

Procedure: 1) Activate lights and siren before entering intersections.
2) Slow and clear all red lights/stop signs.
3) Notify dispatch of response level changes.
4) Reduce speed in adverse weather or dense areas.

Notes: Cancel Code 3 when scene stabilized or downgraded.

laws.title: Patrol Vehicle Operation
laws.content:
Purpose: Promote safe, professional driving in marked and unmarked units.

Policy: Seatbelts are mandatory; mobile data use limited to stopped or voice-directed use when safe.

Procedure: 1) Conduct vehicle inspection at shift start.
2) Obey traffic laws when not in emergency mode.
3) Avoid prolonged in-vehicle computer use while moving.
4) Report collisions immediately and photograph damage.

Notes: Fatigue driving should be reported for relief when possible.

laws.title: PIT Maneuver Authorization
laws.content:
Purpose: Govern use of Precision Immobilization Technique.

Policy: PIT is a form of force and may be used when risks of continued flight outweigh maneuver risks and when trained officers execute.

Procedure: 1) Obtain supervisor approval when practicable.
2) Assess speed, environment, and vehicle type.
3) Execute within trained speed thresholds.
4) Coordinate with secondary units for containment.
5) Provide medical check for occupants post-PIT.

Notes: Avoid PIT on motorcycles, high centers of gravity, or hazardous cargo unless deadly force justified.

laws.title: Pursuit Policy
laws.content:
Purpose: Define when to initiate, continue, or terminate pursuits.

Policy: Pursuits are limited to violent felonies or imminent threats; risk to public must be continuously evaluated.

Procedure: 1) Announce location, direction, speed, and reason when initiating.
2) Supervisor assumes control and may terminate at any time.
3) Limit number of pursuing units per policy.
4) Disengage when risk outweighs need for immediate capture.
5) Complete pursuit report after termination.

Notes: Aerial support may allow reduced ground pressure.
